clue.text: This is why broadcast is unacceptable opinion

indicators.note: something broadcast is put out over the air, so these words are to be heard, not read

parts.note: this is why can be said as here is Y

explanation.surface: A view on why airing something would be offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'This is why' as HERE'S Y (here is the letter Y) and it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is an opinion contrary to accepted doctrine, so it is regarded as unacceptable.

clue.text: Why bridges must bear cross

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the words carry the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why bridges have to carry crossing traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross, in breeding, is the offspring of two different varieties, which is exactly a mixture of kinds.

clue.text: Tries again to pre-empt a student's dry run

indicators.note: to pre-empt is to come before, so the first piece is placed ahead of the rest

parts.note: to rehear a case is to try it again in court
L is the learner driver's plate, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A court retrying a case before a student's practice run.
explanation.walkthrough: Rehears is the legal sense of trying again: a court rehears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice performance before the real thing, which is what a dry run means.

clue.text: It's frowned upon by some purists but one is to happily cohabit

definitions.text: It's frowned upon by some purists
definitions.meaning: grammatical purists object to putting an adverb between to and its verb
the phrase to happily cohabit puts happily between to and cohabit, an example of the construction

explanation.surface: A remark that moral purists disapprove of a couple living together happily.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests purists frown on cohabiting; in fact it is the grammar of 'to happily cohabit' they dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing an adverb within the to-form of a verb is a famous bugbear of prescriptive grammarians.

clue.text: City beach element that is to disappear

parts.note: sand is what a beach is made of
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is
to go is to vanish or disappear

explanation.surface: A city's beach material that is washing away.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a major Californian city on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Excitedly eager to know more since the opening of gallery

parts.note: since, as in some time since, means ago

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Visitors keen with anticipation ever since a gallery opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog describes a state of keen, excited curiosity, waiting to find out what happens.

clue.text: Bemused, blame doubt developing after dance party

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the party

parts.note: a disco is a party for dancing

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters of these two words are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone baffled because of blame and doubt growing after a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused means puzzled and bewildered, a synonym of being thrown into confusion.

clue.text: Be first to support old flame

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting below, so this comes underneath

parts.note: a former lover is an ex
1ST, with the figure written as I, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: Advice to be the first to stand by a former partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To be, in the sense of having being, is simply to live or have reality.

clue.text: Take manual control of extra attraction at fairground

parts.note: over means extra, as in left over
a ride is a fairground attraction such as a roller coaster

explanation.surface: An operator seizing the controls of an additional fairground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: To override an automatic system is to take control of it by hand.

clue.text: Look undaunted, seeing that man sent back inside

indicators.note: inside places the turned pronoun within the other word

parts.note: bold means fearless or undaunted

indicators.note: sent back means turned around, so the pronoun is written backwards

parts.note: he refers to that man

explanation.surface: Someone looking fearless as a man is sent back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing' is only a link here, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Behold is an old imperative meaning see or look at.

clue.text: Scheme of church to welcome new prison

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the church abbreviation surrounds the rest

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: new signals the letters of the following word made into a fresh form

explanation.surface: A church plan to receive a newly built jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PRISON into ONSPIR, which CE takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To scheme as a verb is to plot together secretly, which is to conspire.

clue.text: Conflict in river crossing at the front

indicators.note: in places the conflict within the crossing point

parts.note: a ford is a shallow place to cross a river
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: Fighting at a river crossing on the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward describes a position at or near the front, as in the forward cabin.

clue.text: Lethargy during court case?

parts.note: in means during, as in in the morning
an action is a lawsuit brought in court

explanation.surface: Sluggishness shown while a trial is in progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is a lack of energy, so a state of doing nothing at all.

clue.text: Fatal, having ultimately changed sides to get weapon

indicators.note: the final letter switches from L for left to R for right, a change of side

parts.note: mortal means fatal, as in a mortal wound

explanation.surface: Something deadly that finally switched allegiance to become a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R stand for left and right, so swapping the last letter changes sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortar is a short artillery piece that lobs shells at a steep angle.

clue.text: A church gallery's visual aid material

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A church gallery's material for illustrating a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous group of art galleries in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparent plastic sheets used on overhead projectors were made of this film, a classic presentation aid.

clue.text: Put squeeze on directors for advertising material

parts.note: to sandwich something is to squeeze it between two others
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Pressure being put on a firm's directors.
explanation.walkthrough: A sandwich board is a pair of advertising boards worn front and back by a person walking the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinged placards carried on the shoulders are used to advertise, so they count as promotional material.

clue.text: Hates to maintain lads must eat one

parts.note: to aver is to maintain or assert

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the numeral goes within the boys

parts.note: sons are boys or lads
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Strong dislikes that boys are made to eat something.
explanation.definitionFit: Hates as a plural noun are things loathed, the same as strong dislikes.

clue.text: Remove such a painting

definitions.meaning: to take out or extract something
a painting that does not depict things realistically

explanation.surface: Take down this kind of picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract is to extract, while non-representational art is called by the same word.

clue.text: Liberal lad bit upset, seeing cannons shot here

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A Liberal youngster a little upset at seeing artillery fired.
explanation.walkthrough: A cannon is a billiards shot in which the cue ball strikes two others; 'cannons' looks like artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Players make cannon shots on the cloth surface used for billiards, so this is where they occur.

clue.text: Unusual issue that's likely to succeed

parts.note: odd means unusual
issue means offspring, so a son

explanation.surface: A strange child who seems bound to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a runner at short prices below evens is the favourite, expected to win.

clue.text: Shabby-sounding and singular complement to mince

indicators.note: sounding signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: tatty means shabby or worn

explanation.surface: Something that seems shabby yet unique alongside minced meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Mince and tatties is a Scottish dish of minced beef and potatoes; tattie is Scots for a potato, and 'singular' asks for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is the traditional accompaniment to minced beef in Scotland, using the Scots word.

clue.text: Letter from volunteers supporting article

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting below the other piece

parts.note: the is the definite article
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A message from volunteers backing a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: List dyes for repacking treated artificially

indicators.note: repacking means packing again differently, so the letters go in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to list the dyes to be repackaged after treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylised art is rendered in a conventional, non-natural manner rather than realistically.

clue.text: Appreciates somewhere to stay

definitions.meaning: slang for likes or enjoys, as in really goes for

explanation.surface: Someone who likes where they are lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally one digs music one enjoys, and British lodgings are called by the same word.

clue.text: Drink part of profit — I repaid after getting a return

indicators.note: getting a return means turned back, so the found letters are read backwards
part of means only some letters of the following words are used

explanation.surface: A drink bought with some of the profit, and repaid once money came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' finds FITIREPA in 'profIT I REPAid', read from the end; 'after getting a return' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Bundles of corn accepted on board ship

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so the verb goes between its letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
took means accepted

explanation.surface: Sheaves of grain being loaded on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stooks are groups of sheaves stood upright in a field to dry.

clue.text: Turn, oddly reluctant to cross

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters, first and third

parts.note: averse means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: Someone who turns back, strangely unwilling to cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes TR from Turn, its first and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across or pass over a stretch of ground.

clue.text: Inventor's lack of affectation rejected

definitions.note: Inventor's here is inventor is, the 's linking definition and wordplay

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the phrase is written backwards

parts.note: side means pretentiousness, so having none is no side

explanation.surface: An inventor whose modesty was spurned.
explanation.walkthrough: Side is British slang for airs or pretension; 'rejected' reverses NO SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American who devised the phonograph and a practical light bulb.
